tob-10960: Porphyry, the third-century pupil of Plotinus, was one of antiquity’s most learned philosophers. This selection gathers his treatises on the soul, on abstinence from meat, and on the gods — along with his famous attack on Christianity, preserved only in fragments. Thomas Taylor’s translation opened a window onto the mind of paganism’s last great defender.
tob-0160: Rudolf Steiner’s guide to the higher path lays out the inner training he taught — stillness, focus, and moral schooling — by which the seeker may wake to spirit-worlds. Max Gysi’s rendering brought this early Anthroposophical manual to English readers. The book remains the movement’s front door for newcomers.
tob-4160: Rudolf Otto’s Holy-idea probes faith’s unreasoning core — the dread Mystery, the awe and shudder before Godhead. Harvey’s Englishing bore this latter-day classic to our tongue. The book founded study of holy experience. Its rede still shapes how scholars think on the sacred.
tob-9160: Heath’s Englishing of Archimedes gives the great Syracusan’s tracts — on ball and ring, on whorls, and the famed ‘I have it’ of floating. His edition made number-lore’s father speak our tongue. The work is a landmark of olden science.
tob-10260: The Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy — attributed to Agrippa — adds practical spirit magic to his famous Three Books. Its conjurations, seals, and spirit lists served working magicians for centuries. Scholars doubt Agrippa wrote it, but its influence was enormous. The book became a staple of the grimoire shelf.
cia-0000102960: A July 1987 intelligence report on a Soviet prison work camp listed as Corrective Labor Establishment No. 9, near a place recorded as Bakl. Corrective labor camps were Soviet prisons where inmates did forced manual work, often in harsh conditions. The document is one of many showing how closely the CIA mapped the Soviet camp system late in the Cold War.
cia-0000119760: A September 1956 National Security Council briefing with the latest news from Hungary — prepared for the president's inner circle. When a crisis reached the NSC, it had the White House's full attention. The document is the revolution distilled for the most powerful audience in the world.
cia-0000126960: A January 1965 report on political and economic strains in Colombia — the archive's spelling says Columbia. La Violencia's aftermath still haunted the country, and the economy was shaky. The document maps the pressures on a nation trying to hold together.
cia-0000132160: Situation Report 477: Saddam speaking, two terrorist incidents, and updates — the truncated title compresses a busy day. The Iraqi leader's rhetoric and scattered violence filled the daily brief. The entry is the war's noise, catalogued: speeches, bombs, and the latest counts.
cia-0000132260: Situation Report 567: an outbreak of disease in Iraq, assessed as not from biological weapons — the truncated title suggests the rest. With Saddam's germ arsenal feared, every epidemic was investigated. The document is a negative finding with positive value: not BW, this time.
cia-0000132460: A February 1960 report on Caribbean tensions. The whole basin was unsettled — Cuba exporting revolution, neighbors bracing. The document is the region, tense: the islands, watching Havana.
cia-0000132660: A 1960 report: the Cuban and North Korean regimes expressing identity of views. Two revolutionary states, declaring their solidarity. The document is the kinship, proclaimed: the outcasts, embracing.
cia-0000135860: A 1952 report on the Guatemalan situation. The early file — Arbenz still in power, the plot still forming. The document is the beginning: the target, studied.
cia-0000136260: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LANGEVIN with instruction 11 for broadcasts. The airwaves, directed. The entry is the instruction: the broadcasts, ordered — number eleven.
cia-0000136860: A 1954 cable on the possibility of disturbance at Caracas during the Tenth Inter-American Conference — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The summit, threatened. The document is the possibility: the disturbance, feared.
cia-0000141160: A 1961 cable from JMWAVE — the Miami station — on the disposition of crew members' bodies. The Bay of Pigs dead, handled. The document is the disposition: the fallen, accounted for.
un-ga-res-1760: General Assembly Resolution 1760, adopted in 1962. The early-1960s Assembly spoke for a world shedding empires. The number and year are preserved; the resolution's content belongs to the full text.
un-ga-res-3160: General Assembly Resolution 3160, adopted in 1973. The early-seventies Assembly confronted a changing world. The number and year survive; the resolution's demands live in the full text.
un-ga-res-a-69-60: Resolution A/69/60, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The sixtieth act. The designation and year are certain; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-60: Security Council Resolution 60, adopted in 1948. The early acts accumulated. The designation and year endure; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-460: Security Council Resolution 460, cataloged with the year 1968 — the numbering belongs to 1979, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1160: Security Council Resolution 1160, cataloged with the year 1993 — though the famous Kosovo arms embargo of that number belongs to 1998, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-1260: Security Council Resolution 1260, adopted in 1999 — aligned. The Council's business rolled on. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1360: Security Council Resolution 1360, cataloged with the year 1999 — the numbering suggests 2001, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1560: Security Council Resolution 1560, adopted in 2004 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1860: Security Council Resolution 1860, cataloged with the year 2005 — the historical record places this Gaza war ceasefire resolution in January 2009, demanding an immediate ceasefire in the Strip. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000136560: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136560. The brigade's own words, kept. The entry is the keeping: the words, theirs.
cia-0000136760: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136760. The Bay of Pigs force, on paper in Spanish. The document is the paper: the force, documented.
plos-pone-0000060: A 2006 PLOS ONE study of a large specific deterrent effect of arrest for patronizing a prostitute — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Getting arrested stops repeat customers, the data say. The paper is the deterrent: the arrest, effective.
geneva-bible-1560: The Geneva Bible of 1560 — the English Bible of Shakespeare, the Puritans, and the Mayflower, translated by Protestant exiles in Calvin's Geneva. It was the first English Bible with numbered verses and printed study notes, and its sharp marginal commentary annoyed King James enough to commission his own version. The Bible is the exile's: the verses, numbered — the notes, defiant.
un-sc-res-260: Security Council Resolution 260, adopted in 1968 — aligned. The late-sixties Council deciding. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d60: President Roosevelt to President Inönü — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 60. The president wrote Turkey's leader, courting the neutral. The message is the courtship: the neutral, wooed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d160: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 23, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 160. An October letter filed among November's. The message is the filing: the letter, out of sequence.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d260: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 260. The editors' bridge. The note is the bridge: the documents, spanning.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d360: Bohlen minutes, November 28, 1943 — Document 360. Another session, minuted. The minutes are the second: Bohlen, again.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d460: United Kingdom minutes — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 460. The British record alone. The minutes are Britain's: the Kingdom, minuted.
u-s-copyright-renewals-1960: The Copyright Office's annual catalog for 1960 records which older works had their copyrights renewed that year. Such volumes helped the publishing and entertainment industries keep track of who owned what as decades of books, songs, and films aged. Researchers today mine them for the history of American copyright and the afterlives of forgotten works.
arxiv-2605-08760: Hospitals and phone makers all want to train one shared AI model without handing over their private data. Qijun Hou, Yuchen Shi, Pingyi Fan, and Khaled B. Letaief propose FedGMI, a federated-learning method that uses generative models to perform probabilistic mixture inference across the scattered clients. The 2026 paper offers a new route to learning from distributed data that never leaves home.
arxiv-2605-08860: Constantino Tsallis's nonadditive entropy generalizes the classic Boltzmann formula for systems with long-range quirks. Leandro Lyra Braga Dognini and Tsallis take a closer look at how constraints shape the optimization of the S_q functional — which distributions maximize it under which rules. The 2026 paper is statistical-mechanics foundations.
arxiv-2605-08960: Designing new crystals atom by atom is a generative-modeling dream, but the models need physical common sense. Chengqian Zhang, Yucheng Jin, Duo Zhang, and colleagues transfer physical priors from universal machine-learned interatomic potentials into crystal generative models with CrystalREPA. The 2026 paper grounds crystal generation in real physics.
arxiv-2605-09060: Pointing at the thing a sentence describes — visual grounding — mostly works in English. J. de Curtò, Mauro Liz, and I. de Zarzà extend it with multilingual CLIP, grounding descriptions written in many languages. The 2026 paper brings visual grounding to the world's tongues.
arxiv-2605-09460: Generating images that preserve a person's identity usually takes many slow diffusion steps, pricing out real-time use. Dongqi Zheng shows when few steps are enough, accelerating identity-preserved generation without any training at all. The 2026 paper makes personalized image generation fast, free, and practical.
arxiv-2605-09660: Gravitational waves, light, and neutrinos now arrive from the same cosmic events — the multimessenger astronomy era. Antonio Enea Romano tests cosmological models for consistency against all these messengers together. The 2026 paper cross-examines the universe's story with every available witness.
arxiv-2605-09760: Matching resumes to jobs is a ranking problem that LLMs can refine with a second look. Xiao Yu, Ruize Xu, Chengyuan Xue, and colleagues re-rank candidates with LLMs in ConFit v3. The 2026 paper is hiring tech with a smarter shortlist.
arxiv-2605-09860: Long-horizon vision-language reasoning needs temporal abstraction — knowing when to re-commit to a plan rather than drifting. Chen Li, Zhantao Yang, Fangyi Chen, and colleagues discover that abstraction. The 2026 paper is about agents that replan wisely over time.
plos-pone-0003460: Immunologists discovered a secret protein supply line in this 2008 paper. Cells display protein fragments on MHC class I molecules for immune inspection, and the team found a distinct translation-start mechanism that generates hidden, cryptic peptides for that display. The result reveals a whole extra layer of self-surveillance the immune system runs on.
plos-pone-0003560: Biophysicists found that a channel's helper must sit just right in this 2008 paper. The beta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels tunes how the main alpha-1 pore behaves, and the team showed its precise orientation is critical for regulation. A slight twist changes the channel's behavior, with consequences for nerve and muscle signaling.
plos-pone-0003660: In 2008, Muzzi, Moschioni, and Covacci traced how a germ's grappling hooks evolve. The pilus genes of Streptococcus pneumoniae, used to grip host cells, changed under strong pressure to both keep working and dodge immunity. The team showed selection and gene-swapping together drove the operon's fast evolution.
plos-pone-0003760: Mourier and Willerslev asked if genomes sweep their yards clean in this 2008 paper. Retroelements, jumping DNA that copies itself, are missing from large mammal genome regions. The team tested whether selection against transcriptional interference keeps those regions retroelement-free.
plos-pone-0003860: A 2008 bioinformatics paper taught gene chips to read biology textbooks. The new method folds Gene Ontology knowledge into unsupervised clustering and feature selection for microarray data. The ontology-guided approach finds more meaningful gene groups than blind statistics alone.
plos-pone-0003960: In 2008, Roestenberg, Remarque, and de Jonge tested a malaria vaccine piece in people. The recombinant AMA1 antigen, adjuvanted with Alhydrogel, was assessed for safety and immune response. The trial advances a leading malaria vaccine candidate toward the field.
plos-pone-0004060: In 2008, Reibman, Marmor, and Filner linked a stomach bug to calmer lungs. People carrying Helicobacter pylori had less asthma in an urban sample. The hygiene idea gained weight: fewer microbes, more allergies. The study feeds debate on what early germ exposure protects.
plos-pone-0004160: In 2008, Wang, Lukas, and Yuan examined aging eyes' garbage crews closely. Autophagy and exosomes in the aged retinal pigment epithelium were mapped. The waste-handling shifts may seed drusen in macular degeneration. The cell biology points to new AMD drug targets.
plos-pone-0004260: In 2009, Kwon, Koo, and Zufall found smell neurons losing calcium control badly. Calcium extrusion by the NCX pump faltered in smell neurons lacking OMP. The marker protein's absence slowed calcium clearance a lot. The neat finding clarifies OMP's role in smell.
plos-pone-0004360: In 2009, Yamakawa, Kanai, and Matsumura found the brain mapping warm friendship as space. Social distance judgments lit up the human parietal cortex. Close friends and high lords lived in mapped brain space. The finding grounds social metaphor in real neurons.
plos-pone-0358460: Chronic inflammation is usually the villain — but in the tobacco hornworm caterpillar, starvation rewrites the script. This study found that starvation reconfigures the insect’s immune pathways, producing a state of chronic inflammation that may actually help defend against bacteria. The upside-down finding challenges the idea that inflammation is always harmful.
plos-pone-0358560: Severe asthma in children may start in the gut. This paper identified a combined microbiome–metabolome signature — distinctive microbes plus their chemical products — associated with severe pediatric asthma. The signature could become a diagnostic fingerprint and hint at new treatments.
plos-pone-0358360: The NBA has changed: threes and layups crowd out mid-range shots, and the game’s pace shifted after 2018. This paper analyzed 21 seasons of team and shot-coordinate data (2004–2025) on shot-location polarization and pace stabilization. The two-decade view quantifies basketball’s analytics revolution in hard numbers.
plos-pone-0355860: Dance teachers demo moves facing the class or facing away — which helps students actually learn? This preregistered study optimized instructional perspective for dance learning, testing dancers’ viewing perspective, cognitive load, and expertise. The locked-in-advance design makes the findings trustworthy guidance for teachers and choreographers.
plos-pone-0356760: How Pakistan’s newspapers frame drug addiction shapes public stigma and policy. This Latent Dirichlet Allocation analysis mapped the representation of drug addiction in Pakistani print media. The discovered topic patterns reveal whether coverage informs the public or merely moralizes about users.
plos-pone-0348860: Gaming, scrolling, swiping — when does a habit become an addiction? This protocol lays out a scoping review of definitions, measurement, epidemiology, determinants, and harms of digital behavioral addictions in adolescents and young adults. The planned review will map one of the most contested fields in youth mental health.
plos-pone-0357960: MD-PhD graduates — physician-scientists — aim for the most competitive specialties. This paper tracked trends in their representation and match outcomes from 2007 to 2024. The eighteen-year view shows the health of the physician-scientist pipeline and where it is thinning.
plos-pone-0357460: Lung cancer immunotherapy can bring a tangle of psychosomatic symptoms. This paper combined latent profile and network intervention analysis of these symptoms in immunotherapy patients. The resulting networks reveal which symptoms sit at the center — the ones clinicians should target first for the greatest relief.
plos-pone-0357260: Imbalanced clinical datasets skew AI models toward the majority class. IFC-HFlowVAE is a self-enhancing generative framework with structural anchoring for augmenting imbalanced clinical data. The synthetic patients it generates balance the scales, letting models learn fairly from rare conditions too.
plos-pone-0356560: Exercise capacity in bronchiectasis differs meaningfully between men and women. This South Asian cohort study examined physical activity, sex differences, and functional exercise capacity in bronchiectasis patients. The insights help tailor pulmonary rehabilitation to each patient’s reality.
plos-pone-0356460: In suicide care, the quality of nursing documentation can be a matter of life and death. This qualitative study explored the multilevel determinants of nursing documentation quality in suicide care across Iranian hospitals. The findings point to concrete improvements for records that must never fail.
plos-pone-0355160: Stroke survivors need rehabilitation that reaches into their homes. The TARGeT protocol — Technology-Assisted Rehabilitation Gym for at-home Training — will evaluate feasibility, safety, usability, and clinical promise for stroke survivors. The planned study aims to bring the rehab gym home.
plos-pone-0357660: HIV patients in Ethiopia battle intestinal parasites on top of the virus. This study measured the prevalence of intestinal parasites and associated factors among patients receiving antiretroviral therapy at public hospitals in North Shoa Zone, Oromia. The data guide targeted deworming alongside HIV care.
plos-pone-0351160: Ticks don’t quest randomly — they follow seasonal and geographic rhythms. This paper tracked the spatiotemporal dynamics of questing activity by four tick species across the central Great Plains. The activity patterns inform when and where tick-borne disease risk peaks.
plos-pone-0357360: What keeps educational supervisors professionally committed through the grind? This paper explored the roles of psychological capital, psychological empowerment, and professional competence. The identified factors give institutions a blueprint for developing — and retaining — strong educational leaders.
plos-pone-0356360: The NeuroGAP-Psychosis study is mapping the genetics of psychosis in African populations — historically excluded from such research. This descriptive paper laid out the demographic and clinical characteristics of its participants. The cohort description underpins one of psychiatry’s most important equity efforts.
plos-pone-0356260: Spotting cracked or damaged insulators on power lines in bad weather is a job for AI. This paper built an insulator defect detection method for transmission lines in complex weather, based on an improved YOLOv8n model. The hardened detector keeps working through rain, fog, and glare.
plos-pone-0355960: Automated guided vehicles must navigate chaotic warehouses without colliding. This paper proposed a cooperative trajectory optimization strategy based on SMF-MPC for AGV navigation in complex environments. The cooperative planning lets robot fleets thread through clutter smoothly and safely.
plos-pone-0349360: Preclinical micro-CT researchers need to know their filters’ resolution-noise trade-offs. This paper characterized the resolution–noise characteristics of common FDK filter kernels as a practical reference. The reference data let imaging scientists choose filters with eyes open — no more guessing.
plos-pone-0355560: Asia’s farms must feed billions while the energy transition reshapes everything around them. This paper examined how renewable energy, ICT, financial development, natural resources, institutional quality, and agricultural productivity interact across Asia. The sweeping analysis reveals which combinations of technology, money, and governance actually grow more food — essential intelligence for the continent’s agricultural future.
plos-pone-0354160: Preventing chronic disease in Ethiopia’s Amhara region starts with health literacy. This qualitative study explored adults’ health literacy on non-communicable disease prevention in the northwest region. The findings reveal what people understand — and misunderstand — about the diseases now killing more Ethiopians than infections.
plos-pone-0356060: Children on HIV treatment in Zambia’s Mulobezi and Sesheke districts face a second scourge: intestinal worms. This paper measured the prevalence and determinants of soil-transmitted helminth infections among children on HAART. The findings demand integrated care — because antiretrovirals alone can’t overcome parasites.
plos-pone-0353360: Moving individual fingers lights up the brain in precise patterns. This paper demonstrated brain activity related to individuated finger movement using simultaneous motion capture and fMRI. The synchronized measurements reveal the neural choreography of dexterity — with implications for prosthetics and brain-computer interfaces.
plos-pone-0332560: Australia’s multicultural and rural families face unmet social needs that parental mental health shapes. This paper examined those determinants and the role of parental mental health. The findings reveal compounding disadvantages — and where support services must reach.
plos-pone-0355460: Children’s daily stress is measured biologically in increasingly varied ways. This scoping review mapped the methodological trends in that biological assessment. The synthesis reveals which biomarkers and designs dominate — and which the field has neglected.
europmc-pmc2795760: Combining results from many studies is powerful but fiddly, so these 2009 authors built Meta-Analyst, a free software tool for meta-analysis. It handles binary, continuous, and diagnostic data, walking researchers through pooling studies step by step. The paper introduces the program and shows how it works. The tool made rigorous evidence synthesis available to non-statisticians.
europmc-pmc2814860: Inflammation changes what stem cells do, and this 2010 paper measures the effect precisely. The authors expose human mesenchymal stem cells from bone marrow and umbilical cord to the inflammatory signals IFNgamma and TNFalpha. They find the two cell sources respond differently. The results matter for stem-cell therapies, which land in inflamed tissue.
europmc-pmc2829060: Fruit flies run growth and fuel use with a clan of insulin-like bits. This 2010 paper tracks how the clan split and what each bit does in the fly. The authors chart the clan's past. The side-by-side detail lights how insulin signals gained their many jobs.
europmc-pmc2848560: Molds can duck drug hits by doubling whole gene packs. This 2010 paper catches Cryptococcus neoformans beating azole drugs via spare copies of set chromosomes. The authors nab the dodge live. The find bares how fast germs can redraft their books to live.
europmc-pmc2874360: Drug-proof salmonella in chicken meat reached Canadian patients. This 2010 paper tracks ceftiofur resistance in Salmonella Heidelberg from chicken meat and humans in Canada. The authors' trail links farm drugs to human illness. Their work fueled the farm-antibiotic debate.
europmc-pmc2898760: Whiteflies devastate crops, and this 2010 paper reads their playbook. The authors characterize the whitefly transcriptome from scratch and track gene expression across development. Their data exposes the pest's inner workings. The resource aids the fight against a global crop enemy.
europmc-pmc2965160: Brain immune cells pick their chemical guides carefully. This 2010 mouse study tracks which chemokine receptors central nervous system myeloid cells use, using CCR2-reporter mice. The authors map the guidance system cell by cell. Their work informs brain inflammation research.
europmc-pmc3010660: Sunlight damages DNA, and cells fight back. This 2010 review covers how UV rays break DNA and how cells mend it. The authors survey the molecular battle. Their overview informs skin cancer research. Sunscreen chemists read it for target ideas. Dermatologists use its pathways in clinics.
europmc-pmc3016360: Malaria's mosquito carriers needed mapping. This 2010 paper maps the main Anopheles mosquitoes spreading human malaria across three regions. The authors' maps guide control teams. Their work aids eradication drives. Bed net campaigns use the maps to aim. Thirty-four vector species made the atlas.
europmc-pmc3026760: Worms caught brand-new viruses. This 2011 paper finds wild roundworms hosting never-seen viruses akin to nodaviruses. The authors prove the infections in the lab. Their work opened worm virology. The lab worm finally got its own germs. Immunity studies now use these natural foes.
europmc-pmc3035360: TP53 mutations haunt lung cancer. This 2011 review surveys the fallen guardian gene in non-small cell lung tumors. The authors tally its many breakages. Their overview guides cancer doctors. Half of tumors carry the broken gene. Smokers' tumors break it most often.
europmc-pmc3050760: Brain-wave complexity may flag autism risk. This 2011 paper tests whether messy EEG signals mark autism risk in infants. The authors' findings point to early screening. Their work aids diagnosis. High-risk babies showed distinct signal patterns. Earlier flags mean earlier help for families.
europmc-pmc3052360: Legionella's injection needle got mapped. This 2011 paper lists the proteins the Legionella germ fires into human cells. The authors reveal the payload. Their work points to virulence blockers. The needle hijacks the cell's shipping routes. Blocking it could disarm the germ.
europmc-pmc3101260: Colon cancer's germs got surveyed. This 2011 paper takes stock of the gut germs tied to bowel cancer. The authors map the suspects. Their work points to screening. Fusobacterium topped the suspect list. Stool tests may catch the guilty germs.
europmc-pmc6512960: A human chromosome is a DNA thread meters long stuffed into a microscopic nucleus, yet genes still find their partners with precision. This paper lays out the loop-extrusion model: motor proteins grab DNA and reel it into loops, folding the genome into organized neighborhoods. The framework explains how tiny protein machines impose order on enormous molecules - and how folding errors can drive disease.
europmc-pmc6560460: Medical AI can inherit human prejudice - trained on skewed data, it may under-serve women, minorities, or the poor. This paper examines bias in clinical artificial intelligence and what it means for patient safety. The authors argue that fairness testing must join accuracy testing before AI tools touch real patients.
europmc-pmc6579560: Gut viruses that prey on bacteria - bacteriophages - are not passive bystanders. In mice, researchers showed phages actively remodel the gut's bacterial neighborhoods and the chemical soup they produce. The findings reveal a viral hand steering the microbiome, with implications for therapies that tweak gut communities.
europmc-pmc6634360: The pupil is a window into the mind: it shrinks with light, focuses with near gaze, and widens with mental effort and arousal. This 2018 review tours pupillometry - what pupil responses reveal about psychology and brain function. From attention to emotion, the eye's aperture quietly reports inner states.
europmc-pmc6659660: Light-activated cancer therapies work better when aimed at the cell's endoplasmic reticulum - the protein-folding workshop. This study built a double-targeted system delivering photodynamic and photothermal therapy straight to the ER, sparking immunogenic cell death. The precision strike turns dying tumor cells into immune alarms.
europmc-pmc6770660: Soy's benefits may come from what gut bacteria make of it. Equol - a metabolite brewed from the soy isoflavone daidzein by intestinal microbes - is linked to fewer menopause symptoms, stronger bones, and healthier hearts. This review weighs the evidence for the bacterial middleman's gifts.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-60: This 2007 GAO report takes on the VA's care of seized homes — houses the agency takes back when vets fall behind on backed loans. GAO found the VA barely watched the firms hired to guard and sell these homes. The report calls for a firm grip on the hired help, so the homes keep their worth and the public purse takes no needless hit.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1160: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report finding the IRS could improve how it manages paper case files — the physical folders behind tax disputes and collections. In an agency handling hundreds of millions of accounts, lost or mishandled files meant delays and errors. GAO's recommendations target the unglamorous plumbing of tax administration, where better filing cabinets translate into better service.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-860: The Army could not find its own stuff in 2007 — GAO's report says the asset-tracking investment lacked a joined-up strategy. The findings warn that billions for visibility software would blur without a master plan. An army that cannot see its gear, the report argues, cannot move it.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-660: Air cargo bound for America was barely screened in 2007 — GAO's report says the federal effort was young and needed muscle. The findings flag the flying freight gap. The report warns that the bomb in the belly was the hole in the fence.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-360: The Joint Strike Fighter was inching forward in 2007, and GAO's report says progress had been made while serious challenges remained. The findings balance the gains against the risks. The report reads as the cautiously optimistic chapter of the costliest weapons story ever told.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-60: The Guard's gear gaps needed measuring in 2007, and GAO's report says the domestic equipment needs and readiness had to be identified. The findings demand the inventory. The report warns that the hometown troops should not deploy with empty racks. The weekend warriors needed weekday gear.
openalex-w7204707960: Ancient rock paintings in Tocantins face sun, rain, vandals, and time. This article studies the main forces damaging rock-art sites in the Serra do Lajeado protected area and sets out guidelines for watching, protecting, and managing them. The authors treat the sites as fragile cultural treasures needing active care. A heritage-conservation study where archaeology meets park management.
openalex-w7204531360: Parents who post their children's photos online rarely think about consent. This law article studies sharenting through the lens of children's vulnerability in the digital age, now sharpened by AI that can copy faces and voices. The authors weigh parents' free expression against children's rights to privacy and identity. A sharp legal analysis of a everyday habit with lasting consequences.
pmc-13428460: This 2026 paper on juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM) showed that interferon-related gene expression defines disease activity, organ involvement, and treatment response. The interferon signature turns a blood test into a disease compass. For a rare childhood disease, such stratification is precious.
pmc-13385460: This 2026 scoping review examined how the UN sustainable development goals are embedded in education for the mental health workforce — which pedagogies and practices teach them. Training clinicians to think globally starts in the classroom. The review maps the current state.
pmc-13323160: In this 2026 mixed-methods study, students evaluated a virtual reality animation for teaching drug absorption and bioavailability in pharmacology. VR turns abstract kinetics into something visible. The evaluation reports whether students actually learned better.
pmc-13369960: This 2026 paper prioritized interventions for integrating hypertension management into cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic care in primary health settings, using evidence-informed methods. The CKM framework bundles related risks. The prioritization guides resource-limited clinics.
pmc-13431460: In this 2026 paper, a machine-learning deep plasma proteome classifier was developed and validated for early-stage breast cancer detection. Blood proteins plus AI could catch cancer early. The classifier is the advance.
pmc-13424660: This 2026 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial tested losartan and prednisolone for post-COVID syndrome with cardiac inflammation. The repurposed drugs targeted the lingering inflammation. The trial is the rigorous test.
pmc-13619460: A 2026 paper on pre-existing and cross-reactive immunity to avian influenza H5N1 in humans — implications for pandemic risk and vaccine strategies. Prior exposures may blunt or shape the next pandemic. The immunity data inform preparedness.
pmc-13491360: This 2026 scoping review mapped the clinical, genetic, psychosocial, and care landscape of X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism in Filipino men. The "lubag" disease needs comprehensive understanding. The review is the landscape.
pmc-13492460: In this 2026 paper, potassium-selective nanoelectrode arrays profiled single human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. The heart cells' potassium was measured individually. The arrays are the tool.
pmc-13470360: This 2026 case report described an unusual catastrophic neurological complication following routine arthroscopic multiligament knee reconstruction. The routine surgery went catastrophically wrong. The case is the warning.
pmc-13451560: A 2026 systematic review of second-to-fourth digit ratio (2D:4D) in breast cancer. The finger-length marker's cancer link was synthesized. The review weighs the evidence.
pmc-13532760: This 2026 paper, "Working out of necessity," examined how job lock shaped health for older workers. The trapped workers' health suffered. The shaping is the socioeconomic finding.
pmc-13495360: This 2026 leukemia paper showed acute B-cell lymphoblastic leukemia-derived large oncosomes modulated the bone marrow microenvironment. The tumor's vesicles reshaped the niche. The modulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13186560: A 2026 study of dietary patterns and night work — metabolic syndrome in healthcare workers. The shift workers' diets were linked to metabolic harm. The pattern is the finding.
